#### Workstream 8 review: render-time curve geometry on the datashader edge entry points

**Status:** propose (2026-08-13; post-implementation, against the unstaged working tree on branch `53-scale-hiveplotlib-to-larger-networks`. Live spec read as the "the geometry record is dropped" revision amendment plus Examples 6 and 7; the two earlier WS8 amendments read as superseded history.)

**API surface reviewed:** `datashade_edges_mpl(num_steps=, construct_curves_kwargs=)`, `datashade_hive_plot_mpl(num_steps=, construct_curves_kwargs=)`, `BaseHivePlot.construct_curves(num_steps=)`, `BaseHivePlot.connect_axes(num_steps=)` plus its lazy-subset warning, `BaseHivePlot.add_edge_curves_between_axes(num_steps=)`, the new public `BaseHivePlot.num_steps_per_edge` attribute, `InvalidConstructCurvesKwargError`, and the CHANGELOG entries that describe all of it. Walked as four tasks: render a 10M-edge Dask plot cheaper, get curvier edges on a datashaded plot, mis-pass `num_steps` inside the dict, and set geometry on a Dask plot through `connect_axes`.

**Verdict on the one genuinely new public attribute.** `num_steps_per_edge` on `BaseHivePlot` is the right shape. One attribute, always present, read directly by the three construction methods and by the entry points off the unwrapped instance, no `getattr` duck-typing and no second home to desync. The rejected alternatives (a new base-class constructor parameter, a protected twin behind a property) would both have cost more. The gap is documentation, not design, and it is concern 1.

**Concerns:**

- [worth-discussing] The new public attribute has no documented setter on the class that owns it, and three docstrings send the base-class reader to a constructor parameter that does not exist there — at src/hiveplotlib/hiveplot.py:533 (bare annotation, no attribute docstring), :535-550 (`__init__` documents only `use_numba` / `n_parallel`), :573, and the "``num_steps_per_edge`` attribute, set in ``__init__``" sentence repeated at :1446, :1849, :2221. `BaseHivePlot(num_steps_per_edge=16)` is a `TypeError`; assignment is the only path, and nothing user-facing says so. The autodoc page carries `:members:` alone (docs/source/autodoc/hive_plots/low_level_hive_plot_api.rst:8-9), so an undocumented annotation does not render; today the CHANGELOG (`CHANGELOG.rst:79-84`) documents the attribute better than the class does.
  Suggested change: give the annotation an attribute docstring (autodoc renders it) naming the default and stating that `HivePlot` sets it from its constructor parameter while a `BaseHivePlot` takes assignment, and reword the three method sentences from "set in ``__init__``" to "set by ``HivePlot``'s ``num_steps_per_edge`` parameter, or assigned directly on the instance".

- [worth-discussing] The lazy-drop warning's sampling-rate remedy names a constructor parameter the emitting class does not have — at src/hiveplotlib/hiveplot.py:2280-2283 ("set the sampling rate with `num_steps_per_edge` when constructing the hive plot"). `connect_axes` is a `BaseHivePlot` method, and the library's own test fires this exact message from a bare `BaseHivePlot` (tests/dask_test.py:945-959), where following the advice literally raises. The per-arm split fixed remedy-versus-parameter accuracy; this is the remaining remedy-versus-class slip. The house already has a phrasing that works for both classes, in the sibling guidance at src/hiveplotlib/viz/datashader.py:349-352 ("is set on the hive plot itself (the `use_numba` parameter at construction)").
  Suggested change: "set the sampling rate on the hive plot itself (the `num_steps_per_edge` attribute, a constructor parameter on `HivePlot`), or with `num_steps` on the `hiveplotlib.viz.datashader` edge visualizations at render time".

- [worth-discussing] The Dask out-of-memory failure now has a second real remedy and neither the error nor the notebook names it — at src/hiveplotlib/viz/datashader.py:956-967 and examples/creating_hive_plots_from_dask.ipynb ("Partition Sizing"). - **The `BaseHivePlot` attribute is safe on all four axes asked about.** *Subclassing:* `HivePlot` is the only subclass of anything in `src/` (`hiveplot.py:2408`; the only other `class X(...)` lines in the package are the exception classes). `HivePlotMatrix` (`hiveplot_matrix.py:179`) and `P2CP` (`p2cp.py:21`) are containers, not subclasses, so neither inherits the attribute nor gains an inert one, and `HivePlotMatrix`'s existing `num_steps_per_edge` classmethod parameter keeps forwarding to cells rather than colliding. *Introspection:* nothing in `src/` or `tests/` reads `num_steps_per_edge` other than the four `self.` uses in `hiveplot.py` (`:4112`, `:4620`, `:4674`, `:4685`) and `hiveplot_matrix.py`'s parameter forwarding, so no `hasattr` / `getattr` discriminator flips when the base gains it (the second pass's note that the perf workloads "carry no attribute and take the fallback arm" is superseded harmlessly: they now take the same number from the base). *Copying:* both copy paths are whole-instance deepcopies (`hiveplot.py:2275`), value-agnostic. *Serializing:* neither `to_json` touches instance attributes; both build from `axes` plus a deepcopy of `hive_plot_edges` (`:2320-2372`, `:5080-5113`), so the attribute cannot reach the payload the way a fourth edge-record key would have. *The name collision:* benign in the strict sense, since `HivePlot.__init__` calls `super().__init__()` at `:2693` and assigns at `:2699`, so the subclass value always wins and nothing reads the base value in between.
- **The value-based trigger is precisely expressible, and has no in-tree spurious fire.** Every `connect_axes` caller in the repo either passes `num_steps=self.num_steps_per_edge`, equal to the resolved default by construction (`:4620`, `:4674`, `:4685`, covering `HivePlot.__init__`'s unconditional `connect_adjacent_axes()`, `build_hive_plot`, and every `HivePlotMatrix` cell), or is eager (`p2cp.py:279`, `datasets/toy_hive_plots.py:99` and `:114`, `runners/build_logo.py:98`, the viz and hiveplot tests). `tests/dask_test.py` contains no `connect_axes` call at all, so the lazy arm has no in-tree trigger and the `filterwarnings = error` failure the design was built to avoid is genuinely avoided. `update_edges` never reaches `connect_axes`: it rebuilds through `add_edge_curves_between_axes` (`:4106`) and only for records that already hold `"curves"` (`:4081`), which no lazy subset does. The three non-`num_steps` comparisons are exact value checks against literals, so a float restatement of a default (`control_rho_scale=1.0` against `1`) compares equal and stays correctly silent.
- **The one silent-drop state the trigger cannot see is acceptable.** The warning compares at `connect_axes` time while the render resolves at render time, so mutating `num_steps_per_edge` between the two renders at the new value with no warning. That is the attribute behaving as the instance's declared resolution, which is the design.
- **`add_edge_curves_between_axes` needs no drop-site handling of its own.** On a lazy subset it already raises a legible `TypeError` naming both recoveries (`hiveplot.py:1613-1623`), so the silent-discard hole stays confined to the single site the amendment names.

**Workstream 10 post-grill rubric-check (2026-08-21; planning mode, delta against failure mode 6 only)**

**The headline.** The mitigation does not fire on the incident that named the mode. Run 1's two peak-RSS samples were 14.485 and 13.600 GiB, a 6.5% spread, comfortably inside the 10% band. Its render times spread 36% and its build times 33%, both far outside. So whether the uncapped ogbn run lands in the new third disposition state depends entirely on which of its numbers you evaluate the spread of, and the number the mode was named for is the one that passes. Only the maintainer's separate same-day ruling ("not published at all", now a Workstream 6 done-when) keeps it out of the blog post. The rule generalized from that ruling does not reproduce it.

Items:
  - [must-fix] "Spread wider than the band" names neither which of a child's numbers is judged nor which band, and on the mode-6 incident itself the offending number passes — at Workstream 10 done-when ("Every number is sampled, not taken once") and disposition rule ("A third terminal state").
    Rubric: Failure mode 6 (non-reproducible results underneath the whole argument)
    Push: A child emits several numbers (build time, render time, peak RSS, and for the ogbn runs derived statistics too) and they do not agree on reproducibility: run 1's peak spread 6.5% while its render spread 36.2% (103.59 s against 76.08 s) and its build spread 33.5% (5.14 s against 3.85 s). Read per-number, run 1's peak is confirmed-and-publishable at roughly 14 GiB. Read child-wide, it is condemned. The escalation trigger inherits the same ambiguity and adds a second one: with an exact-match band now living beside the 10% band, "wider than the band" on a child that emits both kinds is undefined, and under the exact-match reading any nonzero spread escalates. State both: escalation and the third state are evaluated **per number against that number's own band**, and a child is condemned as a whole when **any** number it emits spreads past its band (which is what actually reproduces the maintainer's run-1 ruling). Without the second half, the rule as written republishes 11.9 GiB's successor.
  - [must-fix] Every verdict Workstream 10 owes requires a summary statistic, and a done-when in the same amendment forbids picking one — at Workstream 10 done-whens ("The full sample set is recorded and the summary statistic is deferred" against "Every number has a verdict" and "All seven measurement-justified gate constants have their ratios re-established"), disposition rule ("Absolute figures").
    Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: "Within 10% of the recorded value is a confirmation" compares N new samples against a single old sample and never says which of the N. "The measured ratio, the headroom before, the headroom now, and pass or fail" is unstatable without a statistic, and these are Workstream 10's verdicts, not Workstream 6's, so the deferral does not cover them. The tree already disagrees with the deferral: `TINY_FLOOR_TIMING_SAMPLES = 3` with a **best-of-3 minimum** estimator (`tests/performance_regression_test.py:89-93`, applied at `:279-287`), justified in its own comment as the standard low-jitter wall-time estimator, so re-establishing `TINY_FLOOR_TIME_MAX_RATIO` comparably is only possible with min-of-3. The deferral is legitimate for narrative prose and nothing else. Split it: Workstream 10 pins the statistic it computes its own verdicts against (per kind: min for wall time to match the shipped gate, median or max for peak RSS, stated either way), stores every sample, and hands Workstream 6 the free choice for prose only.
  - [must-fix] No band, and no pairing rule, governs a comparison between two sampled children, which the amendment itself says is roughly half the claims — at Workstream 10 disposition rule (four bullets: absolute figures, third state, derived statistics, gate constants), Workstream 6 done-when (the thread-cap pair).
    Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: The published product is mostly ratios: 5.06 GB to 1.05 GB, 0.214, "+46% peak memory for no measurable render speedup", and all seven gate ratios. A ratio is not an absolute figure, not a statistic over a pinned dataset, and not a stated formula, so no bullet reaches it, and its reproducibility does not follow from its operands': two children each spreading 8% inside the band compose into a ratio that can swing 16%. The exposure is concrete on the constant the plan already predicts is fragile. `STREAMED_PEAK_RSS_MAX_FRACTION_LARGE` sits at 0.5 with measured 0.466, headroom 0.034; pairing the highest streamed sample with the lowest single-shot sample rather than the two medians moves that ratio into the 0.49 region the plan itself calls a finding even when green. The thread-cap pair is the same shape: +46% is a two-sample mean against a **single** 24-worker sample (6.388 GiB), and "no measurable render speedup" is a null claim whose entire support is that the spread swamps the difference (66.54 s against 65.38 and 61.86). Add a bullet: a comparison is computed per sample pairing or as a ratio of the pinned statistic with the pairing named, carries its own spread, and is subject to the band and to the third state in its own right. A comparison whose spread exceeds the band is not publishable even when both operands are.
  - [must-fix] Workstream 7 still holds standing authority to take its own one-off timings, which routes around Workstream 10 entirely — at Workstream 7 Files (`runners/performance/...`) and done-when ("Every timing in the table is an honest measured number produced via the harness's WS-B measurement primitives (median-of-N, fixed seeds) on named sweep scenarios").

As written, Workstream 7 may edit `runners/performance/` to add "the sweep scenarios that produce the table's timings" and publish them, which is a one-off un-sampled measurement outside the single session, the exact shape mode 6 indicts.     Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: Finding 1 exists because `/tmp/ogb_run/` and `/tmp/ogb_run2/` were gone and the numbers "cannot currently be re-derived by anyone, including their author". The asymmetry matters: the large-scenario children are re-derivable from the tree, since the log entry names the workload module, the generators, the seed and the pinned thresholds, so prose is enough. The ogbn runs are not. The log records the partition variable, the sorting variable and the thread cap but not the partition count, canvas size, dpi, reduction, `num_steps`, or the tercile and category cut logic, and 4.377 GiB is not reconstructible to 10% from that. Decide a durability standard for the ogbn reproduction machinery before Workstream 10 runs: commit the drivers and `convert.py` somewhere tracked (the wiki repo already carries this plan and ships nothing), or record explicitly that the ogbn half of the published set degrades to prose if that directory is lost, so the choice is made rather than inherited.
  - [worth-discussing] The sampling counts are enumerated by family, so every child outside the two named families has no count, including the most expensive ones — at Workstream 10 done-when ("Five samples on the cheap children (the large-scenario family), two on the expensive ones (the ogbn runs)").
    Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: Three sets fall through. (a) The 10M-edge **stress** family, which is neither the large scenario (2M edges, about 15 s, the family the "cheap" label is pinned to by the 2026-08-20 timings of 14.5, 14.6 and 15.7 s) nor an ogbn run: five children across `STREAMED_STRESS_RENDER_MAX_PEAK_OVER_BUILD_RATIO`, `FUSED_STRESS_MAX_PEAK_OVER_IDS_ONLY_BUILD_RATIO` and `FUSED_STRESS_MAX_PEAK_FRACTION_OF_RESIDENT_CURVES_BUILD`, each peaking near 10 GB, and they are the source of `STRESS_GATE_MIN_TOTAL_RAM_BYTES`'s "peak around 10 GB", which is the one figure the maintainer named as sized-against-by-a-reader. Five samples each is a cost nobody has budgeted; two is a choice nobody has made. (b) The cuDF / VRAM pair, taken in its own environment block; it also needs the per-phase isolation note restated, since RMM peak statistics are a monotone counter and the recorded pair (8,155,022 against 16,315,438 bytes) is a suspiciously exact 2.0007x. (c) The tiny-floor timing children, which already carry a conflicting shipped protocol (warmup plus best-of-3 min). State the rule as a rule (a cost threshold, or a per-child count named in the pre-registration entry) rather than as two named families.
  - [worth-discussing] Observed spread grows with sample count, so a 5-sample child and a 2-sample child are judged against one band on different yardsticks, and escalation mechanically pushes a borderline child toward the third state — at Workstream 10 done-when (sampling), disposition rule (third state).
    Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: Range is monotone non-decreasing in N, so 2 samples of a 20%-variable child frequently land inside 10% (run 1 did) while 5 samples of a 3%-variable child will not look better than 2 would. Two consequences. Escalation is self-fulfilling: a child that spreads past the band at N=2 is re-run to N=5, which can only widen the observed spread, so escalation cannot rescue anything and only confirms the condemnation it triggered on. And the capped run 2, the pair Workstream 6 is now told to publish, sits at 8.7% on two samples (4.377 against 4.025 GiB), inside the band by 1.3 points, so a third sample plausibly tips the one publishable real-data figure into unpublishable. Use an N-independent spread statistic (relative standard deviation, or a fixed N per child with the count recorded), and say what happens when escalation lands a number outside the band: is that automatically the third state, or is it a moved finding.
  - [worth-discussing] The exact-match band compares against recorded values that are rounded, while the precision rider deliberately coarsens the published set that becomes the next baseline — at Workstream 10 disposition rule ("Derived statistics and arithmetic claims get an exact-match band"), Workstream 6 and Workstream 7 precision riders.
    Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: "Any movement is a finding" is undecidable against a rounded record. The 2026-08-20 entry already had to work around it in prose ("0.9615 ... recorded as 0.962", "9.625% ... recorded 9.6%"), and a later re-measure at 9.628% cannot be told from rounding. The two Wave 7 decisions pull against each other here: the precision rider is right for reader-facing prose and corrosive as a measurement baseline. Say that Workstream 10 records every derived statistic and formula result at full precision in the Implementation log regardless of what Workstream 6 prints, and that the exact-match band compares against the full-precision record, never against the published rounding.

**Disposition of the two candidates handed to this pass, decided independently.** Candidate 1 (which band governs escalation) is **confirmed and sharpened**: the band ambiguity is real, but it is the smaller half of item 1, since the larger hole is that "spread" never says *whose* spread, and that is the half that lets the mode-6 incident through. Candidate 2 (a child consuming its budget before anyone learns it was never publishable) is **largely killed**: the budget is a few minutes on the one child it plausibly bites, and the plan has already pre-dispositioned that child out of publication in Workstream 6's done-when, so nothing is learned late that changes an outcome. Its residual is real but different in kind and is folded into items 6 and 7: the uncapped run is still owed two-to-five samples by Workstream 10's out-of-scope bullet while being barred from publication, so state whether it is re-taken at all and what a result could change; and the ordering problem that does bite is not budget but the escalation rule's self-fulfilling direction.

**What the amendment gets right, for the record.** The diagnosis that width was the wrong lever is correct and the evidence supports it, since no band separates +0.1% drift from a 36% same-code swing. The third disposition state is the right addition and its motivation is honest. The split host disclosure is the sharpest thing in the wave: memory as arithmetic and timing as host-sensitive is a real distinction backed by same-session evidence (the thread cap moving peak 46% and render time not at all), not a hedge applied uniformly to look careful. Recording the exact-match band as adopted-on-recommendation rather than as the maintainer's position is the kind of provenance that makes a plan re-readable. The gap is not in the reasoning; it is that the rules were written for one number per child and Workstream 10 now produces N numbers per child, several kinds of number per child, and ratios across children, and the arithmetic of that was never worked through.

Nothing the predecessor raised is re-argued: five of its eight items are genuinely closed and two were dissolved rather than dodged.)

**The headline: the protocol holds, and one seam the removal opened is not covered.** Five fixed samples with no cost carve-out, ratios of medians with the pairing named, full-precision derived statistics, one session on one host, and a version-controlled home for the ogbn machinery are a real defense, and the arithmetic checks out where I re-derived it. What is not covered is that the removed third disposition state was doing two jobs and the amendment retired it on one of them. Its stated reason is publication: "the state existed to protect a convention now discarded, publishing a bare point figure." The Wave 7 capture gave it a verdict job as well, in those words: "filing it as moved manufactures a finding with nothing to find; filing it as confirmed is false." Publication is now genuinely covered by the no-bare-point riders. The verdict is not. A noisy number still gets a binary confirmed-or-moved ruling against a 10% band, and that ruling is what routes findings to the maintainer and gates Workstreams 6 and 7.

Items:
  - [must-fix] A verdict is computed from a median with no relationship to that number's own spread, so on the mode-6 run the verdict flips on which five samples you happen to draw — at Workstream 10 done-when ("Every number has a verdict") and disposition rule ("Absolute figures", the 2026-08-21 median comparison basis).
    Rubric: Failure mode 6 (non-reproducible results underneath the whole argument)
    Push: run 1's render time was recorded at 115 s, so the band floor is 103.5 s exactly. The two samples taken minutes apart on identical code were 103.59 s, inside the band by 0.09 s, and 76.08 s, 34% below it. A median of five drawn from that distribution lands on either side of the floor depending on the draw, so "confirmed" and "moved" are a coin flip on the same code, which is mode 6 relocated from the number up to the verdict. "Moved" is not free: it routes to the maintainer through `amend-plan` and carries a mandated transient-versus-resident attribution that will be applied to a number nothing moved. Do not reinstate the third state; the cheap fix is one clause. Every verdict states the number's range beside its band, and where the range is wider than the band the verdict says so ("median outside the band, range wider than the band, not attributable"), so what reaches the maintainer is a noise verdict rather than a code-moved one.
  - [must-fix] The published spread is a back-to-back within-session range with no stated warmup convention, and this tree already treats first-run cost as structural bias rather than jitter — at Workstream 10 done-when ("Every measured number is sampled at least five times"), Workstream 6 rider ("Nothing is published as a bare point figure"), Workstream 7 rider ("Nothing appears in the table as a bare point").
    Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: two cross-process carry-overs survive the fresh-process-per-sample rule, which only neutralizes the per-process import cost. Numba's compiled artifacts persist on disk (`@njit(cache=True)` at `src/hiveplotlib/utils.py:172` and `:209`), so the first process after an environment change compiles and the rest do not, and this session's own precedent runs `make install` first (2026-08-20 log). The ogbn children read a 1.4 GB 31-part parquet per sample, so sample 1 reads from disk and samples 2 through 5 from page cache. The tree's own tiny-floor gate calls exactly this class of effect systematic bias, not jitter, and warms both paths unconditionally on a measured ~4.8 s cold against ~0.072 s warm, a ~66x asymmetry (`tests/performance_regression_test.py:268-277`). The median survives it (a cold first sample is the max and falls out of a five-sample median). The range does not, and the range is now the entire published evidence of reproducibility, so a cold-cache artifact reaches the reader as "this number is noisy" and is indistinguishable from real scheduler nondeterminism, which is the distinction mode 6 turns on. State whether the first sample of each child is a discarded warmup or a recorded datum, apply it uniformly across children, and record page-cache state for the ogbn runs so a later re-take matches the protocol rather than guessing it.
  - [worth-discussing] "Moved" has no branch for a baseline that was wrong, and the plan's own log carries an instance from the day before — at disposition rule ("Absolute figures", the first diagnostic split), Implementation log 2026-08-20 (the supplementary fourth child).
    Rubric: Failure mode 6
    Push: the fourth child landed below a pre-registration that had assumed float64 curve storage; the probe measured float32 at 808 bytes per edge, and the entry correctly recorded the error as the pre-registration's arithmetic rather than the library's behavior. Under the rule as written that number is "moved", routed with a transient-versus-resident attribution, when the true finding is that the old figure was never right. The distinction is load-bearing for mode 6 specifically: a wrong baseline is the mode firing on the *published* number, and it should be recorded as a retraction rather than as drift, because the two imply opposite actions. Add the third branch to the diagnostic split and name that fourth child as its precedent. Same bullet, second ambiguity worth one sentence: the verdict done-when judges "against its pre-registration" while the disposition rule judges "within 10% of the recorded value"; say which is the band's baseline when a pre-registered value and a recorded value differ.

    Rubric: Failure mode 6 (partial: the fork the grill raised was closed without answering its motivating case)
    Push: the fork was median for narrative figures against max for anything a reader sizes hardware against, and the named instance was `STRESS_GATE_MIN_TOTAL_RAM_BYTES`'s "the 10M-edge children peak around 10 GB", which backs a 24 GB total-RAM guard (`tests/performance_regression_test.py:140-145`). The closing amendment argues only that the verdicts need *a* statistic, which is right and which item 2 of the predecessor pass forced; it never argues median over max for the sizing case, and it binds publication too ("in this workstream's verdicts and in what Workstreams 6 and 7 publish"). A median under-reports a threshold that half the runs exceed, and a reader provisioning a machine against the middle of the distribution is under-provisioned half the time. The samples are all stored anyway, so this costs nothing: record max alongside median for figures a reader sizes hardware against, and let the sizing sentence read against the top of the range. No reopening of the median ruling for verdicts or narrative figures.
  - [worth-discussing] A null claim is licensed by overlapping sample ranges, which is a permissive test for the one claim in the published set that asserts an absence — at disposition rule ("Comparisons and ratios", last sentence) and Workstream 6's thread-cap done-when.

    Push: overlap is stated as a necessary condition and nothing supplies a sufficient one, so an implementer will use it as the test. Two five-sample sets can overlap comfortably while their medians differ 10 to 15%, and a 10% move is a finding everywhere else in this plan, so the same magnitude is a finding on an absolute and publishable as "no difference" on a comparison. The live numbers are already that close: 66.54 s at 24 workers against 65.38 s and 61.86 s at 8. "No measurable render speedup" is a claim the blog post makes, it is half of the thread-cap story ("the knob costs memory and returns nothing"), and a rerun can flip it. State the comparative as the ratio of medians with its range and a bound the samples support ("render time within about X% either way"), rather than as a binary no-difference claim gated on overlap.
  - [nit] The one forced exception to the median attaches to the single constant the done-when does not require re-establishing, and gives no rule for combining its five evaluations — at Workstream 10 constants table, done-when ("All seven measurement-justified gate constants"), done-when (the median's forced exception).
    Rubric: no entry; internal consistency of the protocol
    Push: the amendment counts eight gate constants, seven of them measurement-justified. Reading the tree, the one that is not is `TINY_FLOOR_TIME_MAX_RATIO`, justified as "an expected ~1.0 plus jitter headroom" with no measured value (`tests/performance_regression_test.py:80-87`), and that is exactly the constant the forced exception exists for. So the exception's sole carrier sits outside the set the done-when requires re-establishing, and an implementer counting seven from the table has to decide whether the tiny-floor row is one of them. Second half: that gate's number is a ratio of two min-of-3 wall times taken in one warmed process (`:275-287`), so five evaluations produce five ratios and the gate's own estimator lives inside an evaluation, not across them. Say whether the constant is in scope, and if so that the re-established figure is the median of the five gate evaluations.

**What holds, checked rather than credited.** The flat five with no carve-out is the right call and survives a cost check: the large block is four children at about 15 s each, so five samples is roughly five minutes, and the amendment's nine-minute figure for a five-sample ogbn run is right; the stress family is the only genuinely expensive part and the maintainer priced it knowingly. Ratio-of-medians closes the pairing exposure exactly as claimed, and the worst-case pairing on `STREAMED_PEAK_RSS_MAX_FRACTION_LARGE` re-derives the way the amendment says it does. The two-entry pre-registration ordering, the one-session invariant and the `hiveplotlib-ogbn-profiling` repository are the strongest parts of the protocol and they defend the half of mode 6 that actually fired, a number nobody could re-derive. One thing worth stating plainly because it could be misread as a gap and is not: five back-to-back samples measure within-session repeatability, not cross-session reproducibility, but the plan already carries the cross-session test as the band comparison of this session's median against a months-old recorded value. That is a coherent two-part defense. The exposure is only that what reaches the reader is the within-session half, which is what items 1 and 2 bite.

  self.num_steps_per_edge` (`hiveplot.py:2278`), and all three `connect_adjacent_axes`
  forwards pass `self.num_steps_per_edge` (`:4686`, `:4740`, `:4751`), so the arm is
  structurally unreachable there. Every other in-tree `connect_axes` caller is eager
  (`p2cp.py:273`, `datasets/toy_hive_plots.py:99` / `:114`), so no library-internal call can
  fire the warning at all, which also means the `stacklevel=2` choice can never point above
  a user frame. Float restatement of a default compares equal (`control_rho_scale=1.0`
  against `1`, `:2289`) and stays correctly silent.
- **Eager whitelist validation: holds, first statement of both entry points**
  (`viz/datashader.py:1096-1098`, `:1690-1692`), ahead of `input_check`, figure creation and
  canvas. The lazy test asserts the exception class comes back with `__cause__ is None` and
  no figure was created, parametrized over both a populated lazy subset and the all-empty
  one whose builder never runs (tests/dask_test.py:1185-1226), which is the branch my
  cold-pass MF2 said would otherwise never validate at all.
- **Never persist, never delete: holds, and asserted by identity, not by value.**
  `_chunk_edge_curves` returns the stored array or a fresh one and writes nothing
  (`viz/datashader.py:457-466`); the test captures the pre-render arrays, asserts
  `... is curves` per subset plus contents, then re-renders and asserts the original raster
  comes back (tests/datashader_test.py:1899-1926). The P2CP test does the same on the stored

  (`:425-427` for the trigger, splat at `:464-465` and `:797-799`), covered on the single-shot
  route, the streamed route (parametrized `stream_chunk_threshold=[None, 0]`) and the lazy
  route. The prose describing it is the must-fix above.
- **P2CP raster-identical to a `build_edges(num_steps=N)` twin: holds**, and the test also

  (tests/hiveplot_test.py:2607), true by construction now that the signature references the
  constant instead of a literal; it is a cheap forward guard, not a false positive, and I am
  not asking for it back.

Interactions the tests do not cover, walked by hand, all clean:

  `to_json` implementations keep their deepcopy-and-convert shape (`hiveplot.py:2368`,
  `:5122`) and neither reads instance attributes, and there is no `from_json`, so the new

- **`update_edges`: untouched and not made worse.** It still rebuilds through

  `edge_record.get("ids")` (`viz/datashader.py:1174-1185`), so a subset holding curves and no

  (`viz/hiveplot_matrix.py:215-219`, `:60`), and because resolution now happens once per

  nothing about axis identity or tag; the repeat branch forwards the attribute like the

- **Staleness sweep completes:** a grep over `src/` for "bit for bit", "default construction
  parameters" and "build at defaults" returns nothing.

  bullet (`:29-31`), the render-time parameters folded into the ids-only bullet (`:44-47`),
  and the `Changed` entry for the three methods now honoring `num_steps_per_edge`

Completeness walk behind concern 1, since "are there rebuild paths nobody enumerated?" was the
question I was asked and the answer is load-bearing for the one-word gate:

- **The nine-entry battery is complete for rebuild.** Beyond the seven mutators plus
  `build_hive_plot` and `update_edge_plotting_keyword_arguments(rebuild_edges=True)`, the only
  other `connect_adjacent_axes` callers are `rename_edge_kwargs` (:5160) and the
  `edge_kwarg_hierarchy` setter (:5213), both hard-coded to `rebuild_edges=False`; I read that
  branch rather than trusting the plan's feasibility (a), and it calls `add_edge_kwargs` only
  (:4840-4859, :4881-4913), never `connect_axes`. `HivePlotMatrix.unify_axes` reaches
  `update_axis` per cell (:1034-1042) and `update_all_edge_plotting_keyword_arguments` delegates
  to the per-cell method, so both inherit the battery. All six matrix `HivePlot(...)`
  construction sites forward the parameter (grep-confirmed: :1378, :1406, :1801, :1850, :1897,
  :2240 are the only six in the file).
- **The interactions I was asked about all hold.** `copy()` is a whole-instance `deepcopy`
  (:2445-2451), so a `bool` rides for free. `place_nodes_on_axis` and `reset_edges` are the two
  routes into the ids-only state that predate the flag and both still work, and the `to_json`
  test suite reaches the guard through the first of them. Repeat axes are in the battery fixture
  (`repeat_axes=True`). P2CP is genuinely untouched and cannot reach the flag: `input_check`
  resolves a P2CP to its internal `BaseHivePlot` (viz/input_checks.py:41-43), which now carries
  `persist_curves`, so `unconstructed_curves_check`'s new attribute read cannot `AttributeError`
  on the P2CP path. All four vector backends get the cost clause and the conditional policy
  clause from one helper, with a test each.
- **The memory claim's evidence is sufficient as shipped, and I say so having argued for the
  opposite shape twice.** The structural assertion is stronger than the ratio gate I asked for in
  cold must-fix 3 and delta item 3, for a reason I did not state at the time: `persist_curves=
  False` does not build-then-drop, it never enters `add_edge_curves_between_axes` at all, so
  there is no transient for an RSS number to catch that the structural check misses. What the
  structural check does catch is the only way the claim could be false in code (a render quietly
  persisting its chunks), and `tests/datashader_test.py:2417-2444` checks that before *and*
  after a render on both rasterization routes with a non-vacuous default twin. Non-vacuity is
  real, not decorative: `_assert_curve_persistence` (tests/hiveplot_test.py:8074-8102) fails on
  an empty record set in both directions and asserts `holding_curves == holding_ids` on the
  persisting arm, so an inert gate, an inverted gate, or a fixture that lost its edges all go
  red. What the structural assertion cannot do is produce the number WS6 and WS7 publish; the
  revision parks that as a one-off at WS6 and the Implementation log correctly records it as not
  done. That parking is the right call and I am not reopening it.
- **On the 100% figure.** 4691 statements / 0 missed is line coverage and proves nothing about
  assertion quality on its own; I spot-checked the places where an inert feature could hide
  instead. It cannot: the drop test asserts `expected=not drop_existing_curves` over all four
  combinations, the WS8 composition test asserts the 16-step render *differs* from the same
  instance's default rate (tests/datashader_test.py:2487-2493) so the rate cannot pass by
  coincidence, and every `persist_curves=False` assertion has a default-constructed twin running
  the identical walk. The one thing coverage genuinely cannot see is concern 3's conjunct.

Checks that came back clean, so they are not concerns. Deliberately narrower than the pass above,
which already walked the rebuild-path completeness question; these are the things I re-tested
against the shipped commit because the dispatch named them.

- **The rebuild battery is real and cannot pass on nothing.** `_REBUILD_PATHS`
  (tests/hiveplot_test.py:7996-8024) carries all nine entries, parametrized against both settings,
  and `_assert_curve_persistence` (:8074-8102) fails outright on an empty record set *and* asserts
  `holding_curves == holding_ids` on the persisting arm. This is the WS8 lesson applied: the
  fixture cannot make both readings pass, because the twin runs the identical walk in the other
  direction. The same guard shape appears in datashader_test's `_assert_curves_persisted`
  (:2340-2351), which is what keeps `_assert_no_curves_persisted` from being vacuous even though
  that helper carries no length check of its own.
- **`drop_existing_curves` reaches nothing it should not, including through the shared `Edges`.**
  The traversal (hiveplot.py:1991-1996) is the unscoped form, correctly *without*
  `place_nodes_on_axis`'s `a0 == axis_id` filter, and touches only `"curves"` keys.
  tests/hiveplot_test.py:8284-8328 pins ids, edge kwargs and `relevant_edges` byte-equal across all
  four parameter combinations; tests/hiveplot_matrix_test.py:2235-2273 proves a per-cell drop does
  not reach a sibling that shares the same underlying edge frame. The empty-subset corner is
  covered too (:8446-8483), with the persisting twin storing a zero-row curve array and
  serializing, which is what makes the `to_json` guard's edge-count-blindness correct rather than
  accidental.
- **`update_edges`'s geometry half can never re-persist on a non-persisting instance.** `found_edges`
  is ids-keyed with the `LazyEdgeSubset` arm first (:4343-4346); `found_curves` requires an existing
  `"curves"` entry (:4353-4357) and is the sole gate on the rebuild (:4371). With no curves stored
  there is nothing to rebuild and no path to `add_edge_curves_between_axes`, which is the property
  the split was designed for and it holds structurally, not by test.
- **The phrase-list sweep is complete.** All four phrases grep clean: every surviving occurrence of
  "assembled with `add_edge_ids()` alone", "the resident-memory lever there is", "redraw every edge
  from scratch" and "`add_edge_ids()` without `construct_curves()`" names `persist_curves` or
  `set_persist_curves` in the same paragraph (viz/datashader.py:1039-1056, :1629-1646, :1716;
  hiveplot.py:1889-1893; exceptions/hive_plot.py:96-99; CHANGELOG.rst:39-43).
- **P2CP is still unreachable, with one note worth recording rather than acting on.** Feasibility
  (d)'s claim holds: no public call sequence produces an ids-only P2CP, so `p2cp.py`'s unguarded
  `"curves"` read stays correctly unguarded and the 100%-coverage argument against adding a guard
  is unchanged. The note is that WS9 shortens the private route to that state from hand-mutating
  the record dict to `p2cp._hiveplot.set_persist_curves(False)` plus `build_edges()`. Still a
  private-attribute poke, still not a defect, and I am not proposing the guard the plan already
  ruled out; recorded only so the next reader of feasibility (d) knows the route moved.

## Workstreams

Workstreams are sequenced as a dependency chain. Each is its own MR with its own validation; each is gated by the separate performance-regression harness plan (`wiki/wiki/plans/performance-regression-harness.md`), which is sequenced first. The original A/B/C workstreams map forward as: A → Workstream 2, B → Workstream 4, C → Workstream 5; Workstreams 1 (membership storage) and 3 (fused build) are new.

### Workstream 1: Membership storage redesign (sparse integer indices)

**Status:** shipped — commit `608575e` on branch `53-scale-hiveplotlib-to-larger-networks` (2026-07-03); full gate battery green (adversary must-fix-free, qa pass)
**Depends on:** performance-regression harness (gating only). No in-plan workstream dependency; this ships first in the chain.
**Files:**
- `src/hiveplotlib/hiveplot.py:893` (def) / `:958` (store site) (`BaseHivePlot.__store_edge_ids`; change `relevant_edges[a1][a2][tag]` storage from boolean mask to integer indices of selected edges)
- **All six read sites, moved in lockstep to positional takes** (grep-verified 2026-07-03; re-grep `relevant_edges` in `src/` at dispatch rather than trusting these line refs): `src/hiveplotlib/viz/matplotlib.py:460-463`, `src/hiveplotlib/viz/bokeh.py:580-581`, `src/hiveplotlib/viz/plotly.py:726-729` + `:774-776`, `src/hiveplotlib/viz/holoviews.py:636-637`, `src/hiveplotlib/viz/datashader.py:203-204`, `src/hiveplotlib/hiveplot.py:4650-4655` (`to_json`)
- Seventh consumer, added on master after WS-1 shipped (added by `edge-coverage-and-gotchas-docs.md` WS-A, 2026-07-06): `Edges._drawn_count()` (`src/hiveplotlib/edges.py`) normalizes `relevant_edges` cell values for `BaseHivePlot.edge_coverage`; at the !36 lockstep reconcile, swap its boolean-mask branch to the index-array branch (`len(reduce(np.union1d, arrays))`). It counts without indexing a DataFrame, so WS-1's positional-take rule does not apply to it. Its two direct `test_drawn_count_*` tests (`tests/edges_test.py`) plant boolean masks into cells and swap to planted index arrays with the helper body; a miss there is loud, not silent (`np.union1d` over planted bools fails both).
- Verify-not-break (value-type-agnostic): `src/hiveplotlib/edges.py:244-256` (`Edges.copy()` deepcopy + docstring wording), `src/hiveplotlib/hiveplot_matrix.py:693` (shared matrix-cell reference), `src/hiveplotlib/hiveplot.py:782-835` (reset/pop bookkeeping)
- `tests/hiveplot_test.py`, `tests/viz/datashader_test.py`, and the sibling backend test files as needed (assert membership round-trips correctly; assert storage is integer-index-shaped, not full-length-bool-shaped; non-RangeIndex coverage per done-when)
- `CHANGELOG.rst` (entry for the storage change)

**Done when:**
- `relevant_edges[a1][a2][tag]` stores integer indices of the selected edges, not a full-length boolean mask. Total membership storage across all axis-pairs is O(num_edges), not O(num_pairs × num_edges).
- **Every** `relevant_edges` read site moves in lockstep (the six verified sites in Files: matplotlib, bokeh, plotly ×2, holoviews, datashader, `to_json`), producing byte-identical output across **all** backends — not just datashader — and identical `to_json` output vs. pre-change behavior on the existing test suites.
- **Positional-indexing rule at every read site (2026-07-03):** the integer indices are applied positionally (`.iloc[idx]` / `.take(idx)`), never label-based and never bare bracket selection — `.loc[int_array]` selects by label (wrong rows or KeyError on non-RangeIndex frames) and `df[int_array]` is column selection. No read site may keep `.loc` / `df[...]` selection over the new integer indices.
- **Non-RangeIndex test coverage (Failure mode 4):** the test matrix includes edge frames with a non-default index (at minimum a shuffled/offset integer index; a string index too if cheap), asserting identical selections/output vs. the same data on a RangeIndex, so label/positional divergence cannot pass green.
- All existing tests pass with no regressions (the change is internal; no public entry point moves — but note `relevant_edges` is a non-underscored attribute, so its stored value type changing is the one user-visible edge, carried by the CHANGELOG entry).
- A test asserts the stored value is integer indices (length == number of selected edges) rather than a full-length boolean array, on a multi-axis-pair graph. The index dtype is an explicit implementer decision recorded in the Implementation log (int32 vs int64; the O() claim is dtype-independent, byte-level comparisons are not).
- The in-RAM storage structure is designed to admit the Dask non-materializing equivalent that Workstream 5 supplies (the integer-index choice here is the in-RAM half of one storage decision spanning both workstreams; document the intended Dask counterpart in a code comment or the Implementation log so Workstream 5 does not redesign it).
- Harness-gated validation: the performance-regression harness confirms no speed regression on the standard sweep and records the in-RAM membership-storage delta on a multi-axis-pair graph. Expectation set honestly (2026-07-03): the delta is MBs against the curves' GBs and can go either direction depending on dtype and axis count; WS1's value is structural, so the gate is no-speed-regression plus a recorded delta, not a headline memory reduction.
- CHANGELOG entry added.

**Interactions:** see "Cross-workstream performance interactions" §4 (WS4 must re-express the integer-index gather through narwhals; do not bake pandas `.iloc`-specific assumptions into it) and §3 (the integer-index structure is extended, not redesigned, by WS5's Dask non-materializing storage).

### Workstream 2: Reduction-aware chunked rasterization (datashader backend)

**Status:** shipped — commit `413b743` on branch `53-scale-hiveplotlib-to-larger-networks` (2026-07-03); dormant gates armed + canary deleted; adversary must-fix (streamed-mean NaN denominator) fixed and CLOSED same day; api-critic + adversary post-impl filled; qa pass
**Depends on:** Workstream 1 (consumes the integer-index membership at `datashader.py:203-204`); performance-regression harness (gating).
**Files:**
- `src/hiveplotlib/viz/datashader.py` (primary; refactor `datashade_edges_mpl`, `datashade_nodes_mpl`, verify `datashade_hive_plot_mpl` benefits flow through; add `stream_chunk_threshold` parameter)
- `tests/viz/datashader_test.py` (or equivalent path; add memory-bound tests gated by available RAM, and var/std-equivalence tests)
- `runners/performance/...` (extend the datashader sweep to validate at 10M+ and add peak-memory measurement; coordinate with the harness plan)
- `CHANGELOG.rst` (entry for the refactor and the new parameter)
- `docs/source/...` autodoc for the three datashader functions (signature gains `stream_chunk_threshold`; docstring grows a note on memory characteristics and the var/std carve-out)
- `wiki/wiki/concepts/edge-rendering.md` lines 39-46 ("Rendering Pipeline" gains note on chunked aggregation; post-task research-liaison pass)

**Done when:**
- The three datashader entry points accept `stream_chunk_threshold: Optional[int] = None`. Default `None` auto-decides by edge count; an explicit value forces the switch point. The single-shot path remains the default for the common (small) case.
- Reduction-aware streaming with an explicit per-reduction combine algebra over `(g1, g2, tag)` chunks: count/sum combine additively; **`any` combines via elementwise OR (or max), never addition** (summing boolean `any` rasters produces counts); mean accumulates per-chunk sum + count and divides once at the end (reusing the existing density-correction divide pattern at `datashader.py:242-247`); the chunk's curves array is dropped before the next chunk.
- max/min are cheaply combinable via elementwise max/min. The implementer either supports them in the streamed path or leaves them in the single-shot-or-delegate fallback bucket; either way the classification is a stated decision recorded in the Implementation log, not an accident of the "exotic" catch-all.
- Order of operations on the streamed path: combine **raw per-chunk aggregates** first, then apply `tf.spread` and the density-correction divide exactly once at the end, matching the single-shot code at `datashader.py:236-247` (which spreads and divides after aggregation). Per-chunk spreading before combination would drift from the single-shot baseline and show up as near-tolerance equivalence failures.
- **var/std and any other non-additive / exotic reduction never sum per-chunk rasters.** They either (i) delegate partial-aggregate combination to datashader by feeding it a Dask/cuDF frame (verify the pinned datashader version combines moment-based partial aggregates across partitions; flag the version dependency) or (ii) fall back to the single-shot path. `stream_chunk_threshold` is ignored for these reductions.
- Same streaming shape for `datashade_nodes_mpl` over axes (node points are count-based; additive applies).
- **var/std-equivalence gate:** the streamed-or-delegated path produces output matching the single-shot baseline within tolerance for every supported reduction, verified explicitly against `examples/datashading_statistical_summaries_of_metadata.ipynb`'s `ds.var` (×2) and `ds.mean` (×1) usage. Exact match for count/sum/any; division-tolerance for mean; var/std verified against the single-shot or delegated result.
- All existing datashader tests pass with no regressions (visual or numeric).
- A new memory-bound test confirms peak transient RSS for a synthetic 10M-edge graph on the streamed path stays under O(largest_chunk × num_steps × 4 bytes) rather than O(total_edges × num_steps × 4 bytes). The synthetic scenario scales node count in proportion to edge count, stated in the scenario definition — no token node counts (Failure mode 2). **Memory-gate policy (2026-07-03):** on the canonical host (ringtail, 32 GB) this gate always runs — the RAM-availability skip guard exists for foreign environments only; when RAM is contended the gate serializes after the parallel suite finishes rather than skipping; in the auto-dispatch window a skipped memory gate is a halt-back, not a pass.
- The at-scale streamed render is validated as **readable at the raster resolution we ship/document** — the right blob with visible structure at usable resolution, not merely a returned figure object (Failure mode 1). The between-workstream review packet includes the rendered image so the check is auditable in the auto window.
- **Dedicated default-suite unit tests per rendering mode (2026-07-03 testing directive):** every new rendering mode/branch WS2 introduces (the streamed path, the single-shot selection branch, the `stream_chunk_threshold` auto/forced threshold policy, and the var/std ignore-the-threshold carve-out) carries its own unit tests in `tests/` under `@pytest.mark.datashader`, running in the parallel coverage run and exercising the mode directly as a unit, not merely reached indirectly. Redundancy with the harness's equivalence gates is acceptable and expected: a per-mode unit-test failure localizes which mode broke, where a gate failure only says two paths disagree. Harness-lane tests (`performance` / `perf_harness` markers) contribute zero coverage after the 2026-07-03 marker split, so the 100% gate on `src/hiveplotlib` can only be satisfied by these default-suite tests; a new rendering-mode line without one fails CI.
- Harness-gated validation: the performance-regression harness confirms no speed regression on the single-shot (default) path, records the streamed-path memory reduction at 10M+ edges, and the run passes the var/std-equivalence gate. **This bullet is NOT satisfiable with the harness's streamed-vs-single-shot gates still dormant (2026-07-02 amendment).** Concretely, WS2 completion requires: (a) **unskipping and wiring the three named dormant gates in `tests/performance_regression_test.py`** — the tiny-floor timing band, the large-scenario streamed-vs-single-shot peak-RSS fraction, and the streamed-vs-single-shot raster equivalence via per-side render kwargs; (b) **deleting the canary test that guards the arming** (the `stream_chunk_threshold` signature canary in the default suite, which fails the moment the parameter appears in the datashader entry point's signature); (c) **making the 0.5 RSS-fraction (`STREAMED_PEAK_RSS_MAX_FRACTION_LARGE`) unskip decision explicitly against the WS2-alone vs WS2+WS3-cumulative distinction** (interactions §2) rather than quietly retuning the constant.
- CHANGELOG entry added.
- Docstring note explaining chunked aggregation, the `stream_chunk_threshold` semantics, and the var/std carve-out added to the three datashader entry points.
- API critic post-impl review section filled in this plan.
- **Boundary-gap follow-up (2026-07-04 amendment): column-mapped styling parity.** `edge_viz_kwargs` / `node_viz_kwargs` naming metadata columns, plus `to_json`, work on polars-built plots with output matching the pandas twin. The seven pandas-only gather sites (`viz/matplotlib.py:464`, `viz/bokeh.py:582`, `viz/holoviews.py:638`, `viz/plotly.py:730` + `:780` hover customdata, `hiveplot.py:4842` `to_json` kwarg resolution, `:4865` `to_json` `set_index`) are re-expressed positionally through the narwhals boundary (the `_edge_chunk_metadata_values` precedent; internal materialization for plotting consumption is fine, user frames never mutated or coerced). Polars-marked tests per backend + `to_json`, mirroring the WS1 non-RangeIndex equivalence battery's assertions (per-collection styling values / CDS contents / serialized figure incl. customdata / vdim values / `to_json` string equality).
- **Boundary-gap follow-up (2026-07-04 amendment): `add_nodes` through the boundary.** `BaseHivePlot.add_nodes` (`hiveplot.py:621`) concat mirrors `Edges.add_edges` (pandas fast-path preserved; narwhals vertical concat; legible mixed-library `TypeError`). Polars-marked tests: incremental add keeps `nodes.data` polars; mixed-library case raises the legible error.

**Interactions:** see "Cross-workstream performance interactions" §1 (the streaming-vs-single-shot threshold is ONE shared policy consumed by both WS2 and WS3, not set per-workstream; per-chunk `cvs.line` is a small-scale speed regression, so the harness must assert no-regression at small scale), §2 (WS2's memory win is only partly realized until WS3; measure cumulative peak-RSS, not per-workstream deltas, to avoid undervaluing it), and §3 (WS5 later lets the var/std reductions WS2 punts to single-shot stream over a Dask/cuDF frame).

The two regimes are covered as follows:
  - **Multi-process Dask path — explicit instrument SELECTION at WS5 (2026-07-03 amendment; replaces the earlier "inherited from the harness MR (tier 2), WS5 does not build its own" framing):** WS5 selects and records the memory instrument among three candidates. Deciding fact: Dask's default local scheduler for dataframe work is **threaded** (one process), in which case tier-1 single-process exact RSS (`measure_peak_rss`) suffices and neither tier-2 nor Dask-native diagnostics are needed. Candidates: (a) **tier-1** if WS5 lands on the threaded scheduler; (b) **Dask-native diagnostics** (MemorySampler / per-worker metrics) if on the distributed scheduler — preferred where applicable per the maintainer's ecosystem-standard-tooling principle (2026-07-03 amendment); (c) **tier-2** (the harness's `measure_peak_rss_tree`, now provisional) only where an external whole-tree observer is needed: the multiprocessing scheduler (which has no Dask diagnostics), or external verification of framework self-reporting (which matters most for the future autonomous-loop use, where the metric must resist gaming). A small Dask-input scenario on the performance runner must state which instrument it reports.
  - **cuDF/GPU path (WS5 owns this, hard gate):** GPU work allocates **VRAM, not RSS**, so peak RSS misses it entirely. The canonical metric is **per-process VRAM peak via RMM allocation statistics (`rmm.statistics`; exact)** *(instrument amended 2026-07-05: the originally pinned cupy mempool measured exactly 0 bytes for this workload, since datashader's CUDA aggregates allocate via numba and cuDF via RMM; see the 2026-07-05 amendment)* — `nvidia-smi` reports whole-GPU memory, which is shared and noisy (the canonical host already sits ~5 GB used by unrelated apps) and cannot isolate the workload's peak, so it is a fallback / sanity-check only, never the published figure. This regime is **testable locally and is NOT hardware-blocked**: the canonical host has a usable GPU (NVIDIA RTX 5070, 12 GB). Implementation chooses between (a) storing the membership as a Dask Series, (b) adding a per-tag boolean column to the edge frame (kept as Dask), or (c) an equivalent structure that avoids materializing a per-edge array into RAM. The pandas/polars case keeps the Workstream 1 in-RAM integer-index storage. A user with few-but-huge partitions can still exceed RAM, defeating the streaming win. Documentation names a concrete repartition guideline (e.g., "for very large edge sets, repartition to ensure no partition exceeds ~10M edges before passing to hiveplotlib"; the exact recommended ceiling is implementer's call based on benchmarks).

**Dependency:** Workstream 5 requires Workstreams 1, 3, and 4 to land first. Workstream 1 fixes the membership-storage structure whose Dask non-materializing counterpart lands here; Workstream 3's fused build produces the per-chunk streaming the Dask/cuDF path rides on; Workstream 4 routes input dataframes through narwhals so Dask and cuDF flow through validation/filtering without bespoke code paths.

## Cross-workstream performance interactions

These workstreams ship as separate MRs, but their performance characteristics are coupled. The per-MR harness gate catches a workstream that regresses on its own; what it cannot catch is compound behavior, where a workstream's full value is masked until a later workstream lands, or where two individually-neutral changes interact badly. The interactions below are recorded so that when the maintainer turns each workstream into its own issue, the relevant cross-effect surfaces and informs how that workstream is evaluated.

### 1. WS2/WS3 chunking overhead at small scale (the one genuine regression risk)

Per-chunk `cvs.line` is slightly slower than one single-shot call (per-call overhead, less vectorization), so streaming is a speed *regression* below the scale where memory forces it. WS2 introduces the streamed path; WS3's fused build always chunks (it never materializes). The risk: if WS2 and WS3 each set the streaming-vs-single-shot threshold independently, a small-graph regression ships.

Mitigation: the streaming-vs-single-shot threshold must be ONE shared policy decision in one place, consumed by both WS2 and WS3, not set per-workstream. The harness must assert no-regression at small scale after each merge. (Cross-ref WS2, WS3.)

### 2. WS2's memory win is only partly realized without WS3 (masked benefit, not a regression)

WS2 alone removes only the transient datashader concat copy; the resident materialized curves (~808 MB per 1M edges at `num_steps=100` float32) remain until WS3 lands. Benchmarking WS2 in isolation shows a modest memory delta and risks undervaluing it.

Mitigation: measure cumulative peak-RSS along the chain, not just per-workstream deltas. (Cross-ref WS2, WS3.)

### 3. WS5 retroactively improves WS2 (positive interaction)

The var/std reductions that WS2 must punt to single-shot can stream once WS5 feeds datashader a Dask/cuDF frame (datashader combines moment aggregates across partitions). WS5's non-materializing storage also extends WS1's integer-index structure. These compound favorably. (Cross-ref WS2, WS5; storage link WS1 ↔ WS5.)

### 4. WS4 will re-touch WS1's code (rework, not regression)

WS1's integer-index gather, if written with pandas `.iloc`, has no polars equivalent, so narwhals (WS4) must re-express it.

Mitigation: WS1 should not bake pandas-specific indexing assumptions into the gather. After WS4, measure the pandas path before and after to confirm the narwhals abstraction tax is ~0 (the plan estimates ~2% total / near-zero per-op; verify it, since a small constant tax could mask a WS1 micro-win). (Cross-ref WS1, WS4.)

### 5. WS3's "never persist" is datashader-path-only (a backend-architecture constraint)

The vector backends (matplotlib, bokeh, plotly, holoviews) consume the materialized curve geometry to draw lines, so they require the persisted `hive_plot_edges[...]["curves"]` arrays. WS3's non-persistence can apply only to the datashader rasterization path; the staged `construct_curves` + persist must remain for the vector backends. WS3 must never generalize non-persistence globally. (Cross-ref WS3; stated in WS3's done-when.)

### What escapes per-MR gating

The per-MR harness no-regression gate catches any single workstream that regresses on its own. What escapes per-MR gating is compound behavior: masked benefits (interaction 2), and the rare case of two individually-neutral changes interacting badly (interaction 1). That is why the harness needs a cumulative / rolling-baseline benchmark across the chain, not just per-MR deltas. This requirement is being recorded in the parallel `wiki/wiki/plans/performance-regression-harness.md`.

### Design clarification: narwhals usage pattern is pass-through, not opinionated-internal

**Date:** 2026-05-17
**Trigger:** Maintainer follow-up clarification. Paraphrased from the conversation: "Make the narwhals usage pattern explicit: pass-through, not opinionated-internal. When a user passes polars, dispatch to polars; when they pass pandas, dispatch to pandas; when they pass Dask, dispatch to Dask. We do not convert to a canonical internal frame type."
**Workstream affected:** Workstream B (Narwhals at the input boundary), with a cascading edit to Default justifications. No example change required.
**Change:**
- Default justifications: new "narwhals usage pattern is pass-through, not opinionated-internal" section captures the rationale. Bottleneck math: source-dataframe operations sum to ~10-50 ms on a 1M-edge graph in pandas vs ~2-10 ms in polars; total HivePlot construction is 1-3 seconds dominated by Bezier curves; polars-internal saves roughly 2% of total wall time, not enough to justify the architectural complexity. "Always-polars internally" also breaks the Dask and cuDF/GPU stories (converting Dask to polars defeats out-of-core; converting cuDF to polars pulls data off the GPU); special-casing those backends is the complexity cost without the bottleneck win. Pass-through respects where the user's data lives.
- API usage examples: Examples 2 ("polars in, polars out") and 3 ("pandas in, pandas out") already reflect pass-through behavior accurately; confirmation note added inside the new Default justifications subsection. No rewording needed.

### Added workstream: Workstream 1 — Membership storage redesign (sparse integer indices)

**Date:** 2026-05-29
**Trigger:** Maintainer discussion 2026-05-29. Folds the maintainer's "#4 sparse" idea together with the existing Workstream C Dask-storage requirement — they are ONE data-structure decision, designed once.
**Workstream affected:** new Workstream 1; pulls the `__store_edge_ids` storage decision out of the old Workstream C.
**Change:**
- New Workstream 1 replaces the full-length boolean mask at `BaseHivePlot.__store_edge_ids` (`src/hiveplotlib/hiveplot.py:797`) with integer indices of the selected edges. Edges partition across axis-pairs (each edge belongs to exactly one ordered pair), so the bool storage is O(num_pairs × num_edges) mostly-False bytes; integer indices are O(num_edges) total, strictly better in-RAM whenever multiple axis-pairs exist (always). This is the in-RAM half of the single storage decision; the Dask non-materializing equivalent stays in Workstream 5 and is explicitly designed to extend this structure, not redesign it.
- Downstream consumer correction: the metadata indexing at `src/hiveplotlib/viz/datashader.py:203-204` (`_data[tag][mask]`, boolean-mask indexing) becomes `.iloc[idx]` / positional take. Added to Patterns this replaces (Workstream 1) and to the Workstream 1 Files / done-when.

### In-scope correction (Workstream 2): reduction-aware aggregation replaces "additive raster aggregation"

**Date:** 2026-05-29
**Trigger:** Maintainer discussion 2026-05-29. The old Workstream A said "additive raster aggregation," which is **wrong** for `ds.var` / `ds.std`. The gallery `examples/datashading_statistical_summaries_of_metadata.ipynb` uses `ds.var` twice and `ds.mean` once; naive per-chunk raster summation would silently regress those figures.
**Workstream affected:** Workstream 2 (was Workstream A).
**Change:**
- Aggregation is now **reduction-aware**: count/sum/any stream additively; mean accumulates per-chunk sum + count and divides once (reusing the existing density-correction divide at `datashader.py:242-247`); var/std and any non-additive/exotic reduction never sum per-chunk rasters and instead either delegate partial-aggregate combination to datashader over a Dask/cuDF frame (verify against the pinned datashader version) or fall back to single-shot.
- The single-shot path stays the **default** for the common case and doubles as the equivalence/regression baseline. New done-when bullet: a **var/std-equivalence gate** verified against the gallery notebook's `ds.var`/`ds.mean` usage.
- Memory-bound test updated to float32 (`× 4 bytes`, matching the kernel's actual dtype) rather than the old `× 8 bytes`.

### Added workstream: Workstream 3 — Fused build + internal streaming (resident-memory unlock)

**Date:** 2026-05-29
**Trigger:** Maintainer discussion 2026-05-29. The old Workstream A (chunked rasterization, viz-side) only removes the **transient** concat copy (`datashader.py:224-231`). It does NOT remove the **resident** cost: `construct_curves` materializes and persists every curve on the object (`hive_plot_edges[...]["curves"]`, ~808 MB per 1M edges at num_steps=100 float32, ~8 GB at 10M, impossible at 1B). The real in-RAM out-of-core unlock needs a fused build-and-rasterize path.
**Workstream affected:** new Workstream 3; depends on Workstream 2's per-chunk aggregator.
**Change:**
- New Workstream 3: a fused path samples each chunk's curves, rasterizes into the running aggregate, and discards them, never persisting all curves. Constraint: the fused path retains each chunk's metadata column so the metadata-coloring trick survives. The two-stage `construct_curves` path remains the default and the equivalence baseline; the fused path is selected via the streaming opt-in.
- Needs no narwhals (this is the in-RAM/internal out-of-core case, decision (a) case 1 from the Goal). Resident-vs-transient memory distinction added to the Goal.
- If the fused path needs its own opt-in distinct from `stream_chunk_threshold`, that routes back to `amend-plan` for a naming audit before landing.

### Design clarification: cross-workstream performance interactions recorded as a standalone section

**Date:** 2026-05-29
**Trigger:** Maintainer discussion on cross-workstream regression risk. The five workstreams ship as separate MRs, but their performance characteristics are coupled in ways the per-MR harness gate cannot catch (masked benefits and two-neutral-changes-interacting-badly are compound effects, not per-MR deltas). The maintainer wants each interaction surfaced so that when a workstream becomes its own issue, the relevant cross-effect informs how it is evaluated.

- New top-level section "Cross-workstream performance interactions" (placed before Plan amendments) captures five interactions: (1) WS2/WS3 chunking overhead at small scale, the one genuine regression risk, mitigated by a single shared streaming-vs-single-shot threshold consumed by both plus a per-MR small-scale no-regression assertion; (2) WS2's memory win is only partly realized without WS3, a masked benefit, mitigated by measuring cumulative peak-RSS along the chain; (3) WS5 retroactively improves WS2 (var/std can stream over Dask/cuDF) and its storage extends WS1's, a positive interaction; (4) WS4 re-touches WS1's gather (rework, not regression), mitigated by not baking pandas `.iloc` assumptions into WS1 and verifying the ~0 narwhals tax after WS4; (5) WS3's non-persistence is datashader-path-only, a backend-architecture constraint (vector backends need the persisted curves).
