That also closes the adversary's item 6, whose three fall-through sets (the stress family, the cuDF / VRAM pair, the tiny-floor timing children) had no count because the rule was written as two named families instead of as a rule.

**2. The median is the summary statistic, for memory and for timing, with one forced exception.** The deferral could not survive its own workstream: "within 10% of the recorded value" and "the measured ratio, the headroom before, the headroom now" are unstatable without a statistic, and those are Workstream 10's verdicts, not Workstream 6's. The exception the maintainer attached: when Workstream 10 re-establishes a *gate constant's* ratio it uses that gate's own estimator, because reproducing the ratio any other way measures something the gate does not compute. In the tree today that is exactly `TINY_FLOOR_TIME_MAX_RATIO`, re-established with the best-of-3 minimum its gate specifies. That is re-establishing a CI constant, not producing a published figure. Every other gate's per-child instrument is a fresh-process peak RSS, so a ratio of medians re-establishes it and `make test-performance` green in the same session still exercises the gate's own single-sample arithmetic.

**3. Comparisons are ratios of medians, with the pairing named.** The adversary was right that no bullet reached ratios while roughly half the published set is ratios. Ratios are now built from each side's median rather than from sample pairings, which removes the worst-case exposure it named: pairing the highest streamed sample against the lowest single-shot sample pushes `STREAMED_PEAK_RSS_MAX_FRACTION_LARGE`'s measured 0.466 toward the 0.49 the plan already calls a finding even when green. Every comparison is recorded with both operands' sample sets, so its spread is visible underneath it, and a null claim such as "no measurable render speedup" is stated only where the two sample sets overlap.

**4. Where a figure is charted, it is a jittered scatter of all samples, not a box plot.** Five points do not earn quartile machinery, and a box plot implies a distribution shape this protocol has not sampled enough to claim. A Workstream 6 and Workstream 7 presentation rider, paired with the rider that nothing is published as a bare point.

Deliberately not in the hiveplotlib tracked tree, for two reasons he gave: that repo stays uncluttered, and CI runs ruff repo-wide, so nothing dropped into hiveplotlib is genuinely inert. This closes the adversary's item 5, whose real point was that the fix for finding 1 had landed on one host, off version control, one day after the mode about exactly that was named. Workstream 10's own scratch drivers are recommended into the same repo rather than required, on the asymmetry the adversary itself drew: the large-scenario and stress children are re-derivable from the tree, the ogbn runs are not.

**6. Workstream 7 loses its standing authority to take its own measurements, and the ASV endgame is encoded rather than foreclosed.** Every number in its table now comes from Workstream 10's results entry. The survivor bullet naming the harness's `median-of-N` primitive on named sweep scenarios is rewritten (that primitive was dropped upstream, and the 2026-06-27 bookkeeping amendment corrected Workstream 7's `Depends on` for it but missed this bullet), and `runners/performance/` is out of Workstream 7's Files. That also makes Workstream 10's validity-invariant claim, that documentation-only work satisfies the invariant by construction, true; it was false against Workstream 7's own Files list until this edit.

**The ASV condition the maintainer attached, checked as instructed: there is no clash, so the removal is encoded.** His endgame is rigorous version-controlled performance results in the ASV history. The plan already separates that from this pass: Workstream 10's Out of scope names the post-merge `make benchmark-capture` on master as the durable ASV history and a separate later act, so the two were never the same record. Removing ad-hoc measurement authority moves toward that endgame rather than away from it, since ad-hoc one-off timings are precisely what a version-controlled history replaces. On scope, per his instruction, no carte blanche now: if a genuine measurement need appears when Workstreams 6 and 7 actually run, it routes through `amend-plan` at that point.

**7. Derived statistics and formula results are recorded at full precision, and are computed values rather than measurements.** Adopted on recommendation, closing the adversary's item 8: an exact-match band is undecidable against a rounded record, and the 2026-08-20 entry already had to work around it in prose (0.9615 recorded as 0.962, 9.625% recorded as 9.6%). ### In-scope tweak (Workstream 10, rider narrowed on Workstream 6): the two flagged items ruled, and a post-merge re-pin act for the squash decision

**Date:** 2026-08-21
**Trigger:** the maintainer's rulings on the two items the entry above flagged for sign-off, given the same day, plus one addition arising from a merge decision made in the same conversation. Rule 14 fit: maintainer decisions arising mid-flight that modify done-whens on a workstream that has not run, and one named post-merge act.
**Bucket:** In-scope tweak on Workstream 10, with the Workstream 6 rider narrowed rather than tightened. No workstream is added or removed, no shipped workstream is reopened, nothing ships.
**Workstream affected:** Workstream 10 (one Out-of-scope bullet edited, one added, one disposition-rule bullet edited), Workstream 6 (the uncapped-run bullet narrowed). Two older execution-practice entries annotated rather than rewritten.

**1. The uncapped ogbn run is re-taken, and the exclusion was narrower than the previous entry treated it.** The 2026-08-20 disposition rested on two arguments: that run 1's peak is noisy, and that the old 8-vs-24 pair compared two different plot designs. Yesterday's removal of the third disposition state dissolved the first, since high variance is now an argument to sample more rather than to publish less. Only the confound argument survives, and it bars run 1 **from the thread-cap comparison specifically**. It does not bar citing run 1 standalone, where there is no confound: the same 62M-edge graph with 18,958,075 edges drawn instead of 5,954,058, which is the larger feasibility claim and the case where nothing was tuned to reduce what gets drawn.

So Workstream 10 re-takes run 1 at the flat five samples, like every other measured number. This overrides the recommendation in the entry above, which was to skip it. The reasoning: five samples at 70 to 110 seconds is about nine minutes, cost is already ruled not to be the constraint for a figure backing a blog post, and the one-session invariant makes skipping expensive to reverse. Deciding now that Workstream 6 will not want the number, and being wrong, means reopening a measurement session later, which is the exact failure Workstream 10 exists to prevent. Measuring is cheap insurance; whether to print it stays Workstream 6's editorial call.

**2. Derived statistics and formula results are computed once per session, not sampled five times, and the treatment is provisional.** The reading is adopted: a statistic over pinned data at a fixed seed has no spread to sample, so the five-sample minimum governs measurements and these are computed once and checked against the full-precision record. Weak supporting evidence worth having in the record: the prep passes reproduced to four significant figures across two separate sessions on 2026-08-20. The maintainer's caveat is recorded because it bounds how much this workstream invests here: he has not looked closely at these figures yet and may want to change the scientific exploration of the data entirely once he finishes reviewing the workstreams and does a deep dive over the notebooks, and his priority right now is the run times. Workstream 10 therefore records them at full precision and spends no effort extending or reinterpreting them. Any rework of the homophily and coverage analysis is a later decision routed through `amend-plan`.

**3. Branch 53 squashes on merge, so the measurement anchors get a named post-merge re-pin.** The maintainer flipped the setting on MR !36 himself. The earlier no-squash decision existed so he could profile individual commits across the chain; he has relaxed that to a before-and-after comparison, which makes the repository's standard squash practice the sensible default again. The consequence is narrow and mechanical: commit `3b8d0d6` stops resolving at merge, and two anchors break with it. The two 2026-08-20 Implementation log entries cite it as the re-derivation anchor for the Workstream 9 verdict and the ogbn numbers, and `hiveplotlib-ogbn-profiling`'s README pins the same sha, already hardened pre-merge to describe the code state in words alongside the sha so it degrades rather than breaks. The act is recorded in Workstream 10's Out of scope beside the post-merge `make benchmark-capture`, which is the slot this plan already uses for named post-merge acts, and it does not run now: the log entries are append-only records and stay untouched until the re-pin.

**Only anchors backing a published number are re-pinned.** The log's per-workstream shas (`608575e`, `413b743`, `7c0c610`, `3bf0e94`, `a6e1a8d`, `8966c4d` and the rest) are not. They were true when written, the entries are dated, they back no published claim, and rewriting them post-squash would turn a record of what happened into a tidied fiction.

**What the squash decision stales, recorded rather than rewritten.** Two places, both annotated in place with the date and left standing, since each was correct for the reason it was made and the reason no longer applies:

- The 2026-07-03 marginal-attribution amendment's "**branch 53 must NOT be squash-merged**", already downgraded to a preference on 2026-07-06. Its supersession note now records that the preference is spent, and that the **optional post-merge per-boundary ASV series is foreclosed on master**, since a squash leaves no boundary commits there to run it against. Nothing depends on it: the 2026-07-06 update already made it optional and named the sufficient evidence set, and the durable ASV record is the single post-merge `make benchmark-capture` before-and-after, which a squash does not touch.
- The 2026-07-06 execution-practice update's item 2, "no-squash: hard constraint to maintainer preference," now records the resolution.

Checked and **not** stale: Workstream 9's one-commit decision and the critic records that reason from it, which are about commit granularity inside the branch and about what was inferable at the time, not about how the branch merges.

### In-scope tweak (Workstream 10, riders tightened on Workstreams 6 + 7): the verdict seam closed, a warmup discard, and the noise diagnosis superseded

**Date:** 2026-08-21
**Trigger:** the adversary's second cold post-grill rubric-check on Workstream 10, recorded above under `### Adversary's challenge (planning mode)` as "Workstream 10 second post-grill rubric-check (2026-08-21)". Status challenge, 6 items (2 must-fix, 3 worth-discussing, 1 nit), scoped to the sampling and publication protocol the two earlier 2026-08-21 amendments produced, which the first pass never saw. Rule 14 fit: adversary findings that modify done-whens on a workstream that has not run.
**Bucket:** In-scope tweak on Workstream 10, plus rider tightenings on Workstreams 6 and 7. No workstream is added or removed, no shipped workstream is reopened, nothing ships.
**Workstream affected:** Workstream 10 (five done-whens edited, three disposition-rule bullets edited), Workstream 6 (the uncapped-run bullet and the no-bare-point rider edited), Workstream 7 (the comparative-row rider edited).

**The protocol's core is not what moved.** The pass could not break the five-sample minimum, ratios of medians, full-precision derived statistics, the two-entry pre-registration ordering, or the one-session invariant, and it re-derived the cost arithmetic and the worst-case pairing exposure independently. What it found is a seam the removal of the third disposition state opened: that state was doing two jobs, and yesterday's amendment retired it on one. Publication is genuinely covered by the no-bare-point riders. The **verdict** job was not, and a verdict is what routes findings to the maintainer and gates Workstreams 6 and 7. The state does not come back. Both must-fixes are clauses.

**1. A verdict now states the number's range beside its band.** The band is a fixed 10% with no relationship to a number's own spread, so on run 1's render, recorded at 115 s with a band floor of 103.5 s, and same-code samples minutes apart at 103.594 s and 76.081 s, a median of five lands on either side of the floor by the draw. Confirmed against moved was a coin flip on unchanged code, and moved is not free: it routes through `amend-plan` carrying a mandated transient-versus-resident attribution applied to a number nothing moved. The clause: where the range is wider than the band, the verdict says so in those terms and owes no attribution, so what reaches the maintainer is a noise verdict rather than a code-moved one. It bars nothing from publication, which is what keeps it a qualifier rather than the third state under another name.

**2. Six samples per child, the first discarded as warmup, the discard still recorded.** The fresh-process rule neutralizes per-process import cost and nothing else. Two carry-overs survive it: numba's on-disk compiled artifacts (`@njit(cache=True)` at `src/hiveplotlib/utils.py:172` and `:209`), so the first process after an environment change compiles and the rest do not, and the OS page cache over the ogbn dataset's 1.4 GB 31-part parquet. The median already survives a cold first sample, since it is the max and falls out of five. The range does not, and the range is now the entire published evidence of reproducibility, so a cold-cache artifact would reach the reader as "this number is noisy" and be indistinguishable from real nondeterminism, which is the distinction failure mode 6 turns on. The tree's own precedent for calling this bias rather than jitter is the tiny-floor gate, which warms both paths unconditionally against a roughly 66x cold-warm asymmetry. **Flagged for sign-off**, since it raises the sample count from five to six per child.

**The noise diagnosis is superseded, and the honest position is that the cause is unidentified.** This is the correction that matters most, because it is the one finding that says a published number would be **biased** rather than merely imprecise. The dispatching session told the maintainer that run 1's variance was uncapped-scheduler nondeterminism, and that diagnosis is embedded in the Wave 7 grill capture and in failure mode 6. The 2026-08-20 session's own data says otherwise: first sample worse in every render and every peak measurement it took (run 1 render 103.59 against 76.08, +36.2%; run 2 render 65.38 against 61.86, +5.7%; run 1 peak 14.485 against 13.600 GiB, +6.5%; run 2 peak 4.377 against 4.025 GiB, +8.7%). A systematic direction is a warmup signature, not scatter. The proposed mechanisms do not fully explain it either: page cache should give both runs a similar absolute speedup, and run 1 gained 27.5 s against run 2's 3.5 s. So the recorded position is that the first-sample bias is real and systematic, the cause is unidentified, and five samples with no warmup convention would bake it into the published range.

**The Wave 7 capture and failure mode 6 are left exactly as written**, being append-only records of what was believed at the time. What is corrected is the normative text that rested on the diagnosis, found rather than assumed: Workstream 6's uncapped-run bullet, whose noise argument now falls twice over; the disposition rule's absolute-figures bullet, where the 36% swing is reinterpreted as warmup bias without changing that bullet's conclusion, since width was still the wrong lever and sampling is still the mechanism; and Workstream 10's generalization-label bullet, whose "moved render time by nothing" was the bare absence claim item 3 below now forbids. The transient-versus-resident split, checked as instructed, does not rest on the diagnosis; what it needed was the third branch in item 3 of the table below.

**3. Three worth-discussings, each dispositioned on its merits.**

- **A wrong baseline gets its own branch.** The plan's own log carries the instance from the day before: the supplementary fourth child landed below a pre-registration that had assumed float64 curve storage, and a probe measured float32 at 808.0 bytes per edge. Under the rule as written that number was "moved" and owed a transient-versus-resident attribution, when the true finding is that the old figure was never right. Recorded now as a **retracted baseline**, with that child named as the precedent, because drift asks what changed in the code and a retraction asks what the old number was ever measuring. The second half of the item is settled in the same clause: the band's baseline is the **recorded** value, since the question is whether a published number is still true, and the pre-registration is the surprise detector compared separately.
- **Max is recorded alongside the median for figures a reader sizes hardware against.** Pinning the median everywhere closed the Wave 7 fork by dropping its motivating case, `STRESS_GATE_MIN_TOTAL_RAM_BYTES`'s "the 10M-edge children peak around 10 GB" behind a 24 GB guard, where a reader provisions a machine and is under-provisioned half the time against the middle of the distribution. Recording max costs nothing, since every sample is stored anyway, and it leaves the median ruling untouched for verdicts and narrative figures. **The publication half is flagged for sign-off**, because letting a sizing sentence read against the top of the range narrows the maintainer's same-day median ruling for that one class of figure.
- **No comparison asserts a bare absence of difference.** Overlap was stated as a necessary condition with nothing supplying a sufficient one, so an implementer would have used it as the test. Two five-sample sets can overlap comfortably while their medians differ 10 to 15%, a magnitude that is a finding everywhere else in this plan. The live numbers are that close (66.54 s at 24 workers against 65.38 s and 61.86 s at 8), and "no measurable render speedup" is half the thread-cap story the blog post tells. A close comparison is now stated as the ratio of medians with its range and a bound the samples support, "within about X% either way", never as a binary no-difference claim.

**4. The nit, which was a real off-by-one.** The forced gate-estimator exception was pinned to `TINY_FLOOR_TIME_MAX_RATIO`, which is the one constant of the eight whose justification is an expectation rather than a measurement, so it sat outside the "all seven measurement-justified gate constants" done-when and had no subject. Checked against the tree as instructed: all seven measurement-justified constants are peak-RSS ratios, so none of them needs a gate-specific timing estimator and the exception would be vacuous if left pointed where it was. It is re-pointed rather than removed, because the maintainer's ruling named that constant specifically and it is the battery's only timing gate: the constant is in scope as an eighth, and since the gate's own best-of-3 minimum lives inside one evaluation, the re-established figure is the median of five evaluations, reported with its range.

**Disposition of all six items.**

| # | Item | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | must-fix: verdict flips on the draw, with no relation to the number's spread | **Adopted** as a verdict qualifier (range beside band, not-attributable, no attribution owed). The third state is not reinstated. |
| 2 | must-fix: no warmup convention, and the bias is systematic | **Adopted**, six samples with the first discarded and recorded, plus page-cache and numba-cache state recorded for the ogbn children. The diagnosis correction is recorded normatively. Sample-count change flagged. |
| 3 | worth-discussing: no branch for a wrong baseline | **Adopted**, plus the baseline ambiguity settled (recorded value is the band's baseline). |
| 4 | worth-discussing: median pinned everywhere dropped the sizing case | **Adopted for recording**; the publication half adopted on recommendation and flagged, since it narrows a maintainer ruling. |
| 5 | worth-discussing: null claims licensed by overlap | **Adopted.** Bound the samples support, never a bare absence. |
| 6 | nit: the forced exception's subject sits outside the seven | **Adopted**, re-pointed rather than removed, with the combining rule stated. |

**Flagged for sign-off (two items).**

1. **The sixth sample.** Five becomes six per child with the first discarded, which is roughly a 20% cost increase on every measured number, about eleven minutes rather than nine for a five-sample ogbn run. Consistent with the standing rulings that cost is not the constraint for a figure backing a blog post and that high variance means take more measurements, but it is a sample-count change and the maintainer may veto the extra run. If vetoed, the fallback to record is that the first sample stays in the set and the published range is disclosed as carrying a known first-sample bias, which is worse but honest.
2. **Whether a hardware-sizing sentence reads against the max rather than the median.** Recording max alongside is free and is adopted regardless. Publishing against it narrows the same-day median ruling for one class of figure, so the call is his.

**Text this amendment changes elsewhere in the plan.**

- **Workstream 10 done-whens:** the sampling bullet gains the six-samples-discard-one rule with its evidence; the median bullet gains max-alongside for sizing figures; the gate-constants bullet brings `TINY_FLOOR_TIME_MAX_RATIO` in scope and states the median-of-five-evaluations rule; the verdict bullet gains the two qualifiers; the generalization-label bullet's bare absence claim is tightened.
- **Workstream 10 disposition rule:** the absolute-figures bullet gains the band's baseline, the retracted-baseline branch and the range-beside-band verdict clause, plus the reinterpretation note on the 36% swing; the comparisons bullet replaces the overlap test with a supported bound.
- **Workstream 6:** the uncapped-run bullet records the superseded diagnosis and restates the thread-cap comparison without a bare absence claim; the no-bare-point rider names the published range as the post-warmup range.
- **Workstream 7:** the comparative-row rider gains the same no-bare-absence rule.
- **Left untouched, deliberately:** both adversary sections, the Wave 7 grill capture, failure mode 6, both 2026-08-20 Implementation log entries, and Workstream 10's scope decision.

### In-scope tweak (Workstream 10, riders tightened on Workstream 6): the warmup discard ruled on pilot data, a quiet-host rule, and two corrections

**Date:** 2026-08-21
**Trigger:** a five-sample pilot run to settle the warmup-discard flag with data rather than a blind ruling, plus the maintainer's ruling on it and one new requirement he raised from the same evidence. Rule 14 fit: maintainer decisions arising mid-flight that modify done-whens on a workstream that has not run.
**Bucket:** In-scope tweak on Workstream 10, plus one rider tightened and one open question carried on Workstream 6. No workstream is added or removed, no shipped workstream is reopened, nothing ships.
**Workstream affected:** Workstream 10 (two done-whens edited, two added), Workstream 6 (the uncapped-run bullet edited, one open question added). One 2026-08-20 amendment paragraph annotated.

**The pilot, recorded here as the evidence behind the decisions below.** Five back-to-back samples of the ogbn category run at the 8-worker cap, sequential loop, on a host substantially quieter than the 2026-08-20 session:

| sample | peak GiB | build s | render s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4.529 | 5.57 | 70.12 |
| 2 | 4.242 | 3.43 | 67.76 |
| 3 | 4.325 | 3.26 | 66.23 |
| 4 | 4.366 | 3.28 | 65.76 |
| 5 | 4.831 | 3.17 | 66.59 |

Three findings, all of which bear on the protocol:

1. **The warmup effect is real but metric-specific.** Discarding the first sample takes build's range from 75.6% to 8.0% and render's from 6.6% to 3.0%. Build's cause is identified: the `.npy` prep outputs were copied in immediately before the loop, so sample 1 read them cold, which confirms the page-cache mechanism the second adversary pass named.
2. **Peak RSS has no positional bias at all.** Its maximum is sample 5, not sample 1, and discarding the first changes its range by nothing, 13.9% either way. The discard buys real improvement on timing and nothing on memory, which is the headline metric of this sprint.
3. **Peak RSS spreads 13.9% across five samples, wider than the 10% band.** Genuine run-to-run variance rather than warmup, and exactly the case the range-wider-than-the-band verdict qualifier was written for the day before. Good news in the same data: the originally recorded 4.59 GiB sits inside the observed 4.242 to 4.831 range, so that figure was reproducible after all.

**Ruling on the flagged sixth sample: adopted as written, with a stated limit.** Six samples, the first discarded, the discard still recorded. Finding 2 adds the limit, and the plan says it rather than implying the discard makes every number cleaner: **the discard is justified for timing metrics and does not improve peak-memory reproducibility.** The sampling done-when now carries the pilot's numbers, so a later reader can see why the discard exists and what it does not buy.

**New requirement: while a measurement child runs, the measuring session does no other work.** No greps, no file reads, no agent dispatches, nothing else on the host. The maintainer raised the simplest explanation for the 2026-08-20 first-sample effect and it holds up against that session's record: other work was running on the same machine. Run 1's first sample was in flight during a repo-wide grep returning 4.1 MB, which was matching base64 blobs inside notebooks, while its second sample ran against a session that only polled; run 2's first sample overlapped a 123 KB read of this plan, and its second ran inside a sleep loop. The ordering that looked like a warmup signature lines up at least as well with the measuring session doing other work during the first sample of each pair. Nothing in Workstream 10 stated this, and on the pilot's own evidence it matters more than the discard does. The pilot itself was only substantially quiet rather than perfectly so, since light verification commands ran during two of its samples, so the rule is stated with per-sample host quiet state recorded, which makes it checkable rather than asserted.

**Two corrections, both the dispatching session's, both from trusting two samples.**

1. The capped run was reported as reproducing within about 5%. At five samples its peak spread is 13.9%. The two-sample estimate happened to bracket low.
2. More consequentially, the framing that **the capped configuration is reproducible while the uncapped one is not** rests on n=2 on both sides, and it is now load-bearing in this plan. At five samples the capped run's peak spread of 13.9% is **wider** than the uncapped run's two-sample 6.5%, so the narrative may be backwards. It is recorded as unresolved rather than flipped, since the uncapped side still has two samples, and Workstream 10's full sample sets settle it. The normative text resting on it is corrected the same way the superseded noise diagnosis was: Workstream 6's uncapped-run bullet and the disposition rule's absolute-figures reinterpretation note both now say the ordering is open. The append-only records are left alone, with one dated annotation on the 2026-08-20 amendment paragraph that carried the framing.

**Inventory gap closed: the 24-worker ogbn configuration is its own line at the full sample count.** It has exactly one sample, taken as a one-off, so the thread-cap pair is five against one and the "+46% peak memory" comparison cannot ship as written. The direction survives the gap, since the ratio of medians lands at 1.46 and the single 24-worker value sits outside the 8-worker range, but a comparison with one sample on one side is not a comparison this protocol permits. It is measured in the one session at the same count as every other child, not as another one-off, and Workstream 6's thread-cap bullet now waits on that rather than on the existing pair.

**Open, carried deliberately.**

- **Why the first sample costs more, as a Workstream 6 question rather than a Workstream 10 gate.** The maintainer wants the effect explained rather than merely discarded, because it bears on how the blog post is written: "your first big datashader render costs noticeably more" is a user-facing fact rather than measurement noise. The pilot identified the mechanism for build time only, cold `.npy` reads, not for render. This changes nothing about the data gathering, so it is recorded as a Workstream 6 open question that explicitly does not block Workstream 10.
- **Whether a hardware-sizing sentence reads against the max rather than the median** is still unruled and carries forward. Recording max alongside the median is adopted regardless; publishing against it is the part that narrows the same-day median ruling.

**Text this amendment changes elsewhere in the plan.**

- **Workstream 10 done-whens:** the sampling bullet gains the pilot's five samples, the metric-specific limit, and the finding that peak RSS carries no positional bias; one added for the quiet-host rule with the 2026-08-20 concurrency evidence; one added for the 24-worker configuration as its own inventory line.
- **Workstream 10 disposition rule:** the absolute-figures reinterpretation note records that the capped-against-uncapped ordering does not follow from the width argument and is open.
- **Workstream 6:** the uncapped-run bullet records the unresolved reproducibility framing, the pilot's confirmation that the recorded 4.59 GiB was reproducible, and the requirement that the thread-cap comparison waits for both sides to be measured alike; one open question added on explaining the first-sample effect, marked as not a gate.
- **Annotated, not rewritten:** the 2026-08-20 Wave 7 amendment's sign-off-closed paragraph, whose two-sample capped-and-uncapped framing is qualified in place.
- **Left untouched, deliberately:** both adversary sections, the Wave 7 grill capture, failure mode 6, and both 2026-08-20 Implementation log entries.

## Alternatives considered

- **Collapsing `Edges._data` from dict-of-DataFrames to single-DataFrame-with-tag-column.** Walked back during the planning conversation. The rasterization path (Workstream 2) iterates per-tag anyway; the collapse would be a breaking change to the `Edges._data` shape and the public `Edges.data` property without proportional benefit. Not pursued.
- **Polars-only adoption (drop pandas, switch internals to polars).** Polars's wins are on operations that are not bottlenecks in hiveplotlib (joins, groupbys at scale). The interop cost with matplotlib, networkx, bokeh, and datashader does not earn its keep when the dominant memory cost is the curves array, which is numpy regardless of frame backend. Narwhals at the input boundary captures the polars benefit without the cost. Not pursued.
- **Dask-only adoption (route everything through Dask).** Would slow the median pandas case (small graphs, single-machine). Optional Dask via Workstream 5 captures the benefit without the regression. Not pursued.
- **Flipping `bezier_xy_with_nans`'s default `dtype` from float64 to float32.** Cosmetic; every internal call site passes `dtype=np.float32` already. Public-API change without downstream beneficiary. Noted and left out of all workstreams.
- **Legacy `Node` / `dataframe_to_node_list` deprecation** at `src/hiveplotlib/node.py:430-450`. Worth doing, but it is scaling-unrelated tech debt and would muddy this plan. Belongs to a separate plan.

## Holdouts

Patterns deliberately left as pandas-specific (the qa-engineer should not flag these post-execution):

- `src/hiveplotlib/converters.py` — both directions (widened 2026-07-04; the bullet previously named only the first). `networkx_to_nodes_edges` (`:42`, `nx.to_pandas_edgelist`): NetworkX output is pandas; the immediate next step hands the frame to `Edges`, which (after Workstream 4) accepts pandas natively. `nodes_edges_to_networkx` (`:118-123`, pandas-idiom reads on `nodes.data`): records-mediated networkx interop by design; a polars-built plot fails here today — deliberate holdout with a revival trigger (route the reads through the internal pandas materialization helper if polars→networkx demand appears; see the 2026-07-04 boundary-gap amendment).
- `src/hiveplotlib/node.py:430-450` — `dataframe_to_node_list`. Independently flagged for deprecation; out of scope for this plan.
- `src/hiveplotlib/edges.py:151-153, 181-184` — internal `pd.DataFrame` construction from numpy arrays. The user did not bring a dataframe; we are creating a default to hold the array. No reason to route through narwhals.
- `src/hiveplotlib/viz/{matplotlib,bokeh,plotly,holoviews}.py` pandas operations on **internally produced** frames only (axis `node_placements` is the documented pandas seam; curve geometry is numpy). **Rationale corrected 2026-07-04:** the original premise "these backends do not see user dataframes" was false for column-mapped styling — the `edge_viz_kwargs` / `node_viz_kwargs` gathers (and `to_json`'s kwarg resolution + `set_index`) read user edge/node frames and are WS4 scope per the boundary-gap follow-up amendment, not holdouts. **Second correction (2026-07-04, post-impl disposition):** the user-frame `.columns` attribute-read family (node-styling membership checks + hover column lists, seven sites) also reads user frames and is WS4 scope, routed through `hashable_columns` per the WS4 post-impl disposition; after that sweep this holdout covers genuinely internally produced frames only.
- `src/hiveplotlib/p2cp.py:83` — `P2CP` remains pandas-only behind a legible assert ("`data` must be pandas DataFrame"). The third data-ingesting class, deliberately outside WS4's contract; user-facing acceptance claims are correctly scoped to `NodeCollection`/`Edges`. Revival trigger: route its `data` reads through the `frames.py` helpers if polars-P2CP demand appears (added 2026-07-04, post-impl disposition).
- All `src/hiveplotlib/datasets/` pandas operations. Internal dataset utilities; do not constitute user input boundary.
- `src/hiveplotlib/graph_features/__init__.py` pandas operations. Compute path that produces metrics; downstream of the input boundary.
- The `bezier_xy_with_nans` numpy float64 default at `src/hiveplotlib/utils.py:256`. Documented in Alternatives.

## Implementation log

- 2026-07-03: Workstream 1 complete. `BaseHivePlot.__store_edge_ids` now converts its boolean-mask parameter to integer row positions once (`np.flatnonzero(...).astype(np.int32)`), reuses them for the `"ids"` subset, and stores them in `relevant_edges[a1][a2][tag]`. **Index dtype decision: int32** — halves membership bytes vs int64 (keeping storage at or below the boolean masks it replaces at typical axis counts) while positional indexing caps at 2^31 - 1 rows, beyond any in-RAM pandas edge frame this path stores. **Dask counterpart (WS5 extends, not redesigns):** documented in the store-site code comment — lazy/out-of-core edge frames store an equivalent non-materializing membership structure at this same `__store_edge_ids` site instead of materialized positions; the boolean-mask parameter is retained so the engine-specific storage decision stays centralized at that one site. CI-only failure (6 crashed xdist workers on the Dask equivalence twins + a hard segfault in the serial perf job) with identical package versions to the green local env; root cause: pandas 3's arrow-backed string paths are not thread-safe, and the threaded Dask scheduler raced them — every partition frame built a fresh arrow string column Index and every list-label `.loc` built more, dying on the low-core CI runner inside dask's meta-enforcement `Index.equals` (24-core local timing never lost the race, which is why five green gate batteries missed it). Fix: one interned column `pd.Index` shared by all partition frames and the meta per render (identity fast-path short-circuits enforcement), integer-keyed frame construction, single-column gathers in `build_partition_curve_frame` and `_curves_from_id_pairs`; instrumented worker-thread arrow constructions under `apply_and_enforce` dropped 396 → 0, outputs probed value-and-dtype-identical. Full suite 1589/100%, perf lane 41/0 post-fix. Residual (recorded): ~24 constructions per render remain in dask-expr's own projection layer (dask-internal path, not ours); if CI ever crashes there, it is an upstream pandas/dask report, not a revision of this fix.
